newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Election campaign cost next HK chief US$354,000.
newsitem.headline: Election campaign cost next HK chief US$354,000.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Wednesday it cost him some HK$2.74 million (about US$354,000) to campaign for the job in a race that many in Hong Kong regarded as a foregone conclusion.
Tung issued a statement audited by accountancy firm Coopers & Lybrand International which showed he spent precisely HK$2,739,288 of his own money on his two-month campaign.
A 400-strong panel of local dignitaries, carefully assembled by China, handed the 59-year-old shipping tycoon a sweeping victory in a two-part ballot completed on December 11.

Four contenders vied for the historic job, engaging in a U.S. presidential election-style campaign to step into Governor Chris Patten's shoes when more than 150 years of British rule draw to a close at midnight on June 30.
Hong Kong's democratic lobby boycotted the event as a travesty and refused to take part in the selection process.
They argued Beijing had anointed its man early in 1996 when Chinese President Jiang Zemin singled Tung out from a roomful of Hong Kong advisers and warmly pumped his hand.
The defeated contenders, two former senior judges and a rival businessman, have not revealed how much they spent on campaigning. (US$1=HK$7.73)
